validity.recommendation: Keep as-is. Note the 83 km/line is a GEM-derived half-split of the 166 km combined figure MEED reports for both parallel lines; verify against Aramco package docs if a per-line source ever surfaces. P6721 is the legitimate twin (line "3"), not a duplicate.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE (high): Aramco Master Gas System Expansion Phase 3 (MGS-3, ~$10bn, EPC awarded 2024, 17 packages) is a well-documented real program. MEED explicitly names 'laying 56-inch east-west gas pipelines three and four ... EWPS-3 to EWPS-4 (166 km)' — this exact segment and the line '4' designation. Corroborated independently by Oil & Gas News (OGN) Phase-3 coverage and Pipeline Technology Journal (Sept 2025 L&T section-completion report). Not a GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION (high): 56-inch mainline on the East-West trunk corridor = transmission, gas — correct as recorded. DUPLICATE check: P6721 (EWPS-3-EWPS-4 line '3', also 83 km / 56 in) is the parallel twin line on the same corridor segment, NOT a duplicate — MGS-3 lays two new parallel loop lines ('three' and 'four') along the East-West corridor; they are two distinct physical pipes. Same pattern holds across the P6717-P6728 pairs. ATTRIBUTION (high): Owner Aramco 100% correct (Aramco is developer/owner of the MGS). Endpoints EWPS-3->EWPS-4 (East-West pump stations) within Saudi Arabia confirmed by MEED. SPEC: diameter 56 in confirmed by MEED, blackridge, and pipeline-journal. LENGTH caveat: MEED reports 166 km for the EWPS-3->EWPS-4 segment as the COMBINED figure for both lines three and four; GEM assigned 83 km to each line. This split reconciles with the ~4,153 km stated project total (summing GEM's split segments + EWJZG + distribution lines lands near 4,153), so 83 km/line is defensible and physically sensible (corridor ~83 km, two parallel lines = 166 km of pipe). The cited MEED ref literally supports 166 km combined, not 83 km/line — flagged as a caveat, not an error. STATUS: construction confirmed (see status_reviews). Capacity left blank — MGS-3 adds ~3.15 bscfd across the whole system; no per-line/per-segment capacity is published, so nothing fabricated.

MEED names the EWPS-3 to EWPS-4 route (both endpoints verified present in the article, tokens 'EWPS-3'/'EWPS-4') and the whole MGS-3 is intra-Saudi Arabia, so this ref pairs the country/endpoint values. Only the country fields are asserted; the EWPS-3/EWPS-4 pump-station codes are not resolvable to a specific StartState/Province without a route source, so those sub-fields are left blank rather than guessed.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status 'construction' still correct. MGS-3 EPC awarded 2024 with construction commencing Q2 2024 and completion targeted Q4 2028 (MEED, OGN, blackridge). Most recent independent evidence: Pipeline Technology Journal, 10 Sept 2025, reports L&T completed a 120 km stretch of 56-inch MGS-3 pipeline and teams are mobilized on a further 241 km section — i.e. active construction ongoing, whole program not yet complete. StartYear1=2028 (operational start) matches the Q4 2028 completion target. No evidence of operation, delay, shelving, or cancellation. Well within any dormancy threshold; no status change warranted.

summary: P6722 (MGS III EWPS-3->EWPS-4 line '4', 83 km/56 in): confirmed real, correctly classified transmission gas, Aramco-owned; construction confirmed (active as of Sept 2025, completion 2028). Only caveat: 83 km/line is GEM's half-split of MEED's 166 km combined two-line figure (defensible). Not a duplicate of twin P6721.
